spec.name: revert-reason-panic-variants

panel.evidence: Step 0 calls trigger(0), which executes `uint a = 0; a -= 1;` — a subtraction underflow that Solidity 0.8 semantics require to panic/revert. EVM status=revert (correct), Polkadot status=success with attempts incremented to 1 (nonzero storage entry), indicating the underflow silently wrapped to 2^256-1 instead of reverting.
panel.rationale: Both chains compile the same source with checked arithmetic expected. The EVM correctly reverts on the underflow while solang on Polkadot commits the transaction with state mutation (attempts=1), which is only possible if the underflow check was not enforced. This is a genuine semantic divergence in arithmetic overflow/underflow handling, not an environment, gas, or revert-encoding difference, since the Polkadot side reports outright success rather than an equivalent revert.
panel.cluster_hint: solang fails to trap on uint underflow in compound subtraction (`a -= 1`), wrapping instead of panicking; adjacent to the v0.3.2 overflow-checking fixes but distinct from negate-operator case

panel.evidence: For trigger(0), the source executes attempts++ and then `uint a = 0; a -= 1;`. EVM dry-run and committed status are both `revert`, with zero nonzero storage entries after rollback. Polkadot reports `success` and persists one nonzero storage value, consistent with `attempts == 1`.
panel.rationale: Solidity 0.8 semantics require checked arithmetic, so subtracting 1 from a zero `uint` must panic and revert, including rolling back the preceding `attempts++`. The observed Polkadot success and persisted state therefore indicate that the underflow was not detected or did not cause transaction failure. The storage-count projection is not the primary basis for the finding; the independent status mismatch establishes the semantic divergence.
panel.cluster_hint: unchecked uint underflow in compound subtraction allows execution to succeed and persist prior state

adversarial.evidence: EVM dry-run and committed status are both `revert` with zero nonzero storage entries, consistent with checked-arithmetic rollback of `attempts++`. Polkadot reports committed `success` with one persisted nonzero storage value (attempts==1). Since pallet-contracts rolls back contract storage on revert/trap, the persisted increment is only explainable if the `a -= 1` underflow neither trapped nor reverted — i.e., it silently wrapped. The known Polkadot revert-encoding difference (PR #1449) explains how a revert is reported, not whether it happens; here the state mutation proves no revert occurred.
adversarial.rationale: The strongest rebuttal available is that this is a rediscovery of the v0.3.2 overflow-checking fixes (PR #1496), which addressed the negate operator and 'other math overflow fixes'. However, that PR was merged and presumably fixed compound-assignment underflow along with other operators; a still-failing `-=` on a current build would be a residual gap rather than a duplicate of the fixed negate case. There is no env-value, gas, or oracle-status explanation for persisted storage on the Polkadot side. The evidence survives scrutiny as a genuine solang arithmetic-checking divergence.

screening.cluster_hint: solang fails to trap on uint underflow in compound subtraction (`a -= 1`), wrapping instead of panicking; adjacent to the v0.3.2 overflow-checking fixes but distinct from negate-operator case

history.title: Polkadot: Reverts return encoded error data
history.text:
This is a continuation of #1415. `require()`, `assert()` and `revert()` now return error data, according to the [Ethereum Solidity documentation](https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/v0.8.20/control-structures.html#panic-via-assert-and-error-via-require). Additionally, many reverts inserted by the compiler now return the corresponding `Panic(uint256)`  error data, to align Solang closer with `solc`.

The error types known to the contract are added in the metadata `lang_error` field. At the moment there are only `Error` and `Panic` because we don't support custom errors yet.

Refactored revert-related code into a dedicated `codegen` module to. Refactored the `polkadot::errors` into distinct tests, made them less brittle and added assertions for the execution output.

I'm now working on a follow-up PR for bubbling up uncaught exceptions (this is why it's already included that in the documentation).

history.text:
The language server is much improved, and many fixes all over.

### Added
- Go to definition is now implemented in the language server. [chioni16](https://github.com/chioni16)
- The parser has been updated to be compatible with Ethereum Solidity v0.8.21. [seanyoung](https://github.com/seanyoung)

### Fixed
- **breaking** Resolving import paths now matches solc more closely, and only resolves relative paths when specified as `./foo` or `../foo`. [seanyoung](https://github.com/seanyoung)
- **Solana** The `lamports` and `data` fields of `tx.accounts` can be modified again. [LucasSte](https://github.com/LucasSte)
- It is not longer necessary to save a Solidity file, in order for the language server to pick up changes to the file. [chioni16](https://github.com/chioni16)
- The negate operator `-` now checks for overflow at runtime, and other math overflow fixes. [seanyoung](https://github.com/seanyoung)

### Changed
- The Substrate target has been renamed to Polkadot. [xermicus](https://github.com/xermicus)
- **Polkadot** `assert()` and `require()` is now implemented as a transction revert, rather than a trap. The error data is returned, and encoded the same as on Ethereum.

history.title: fix(soroban): reject unsupported ABI types before codegen
history.text:
## Summary

Fixes the compiler-side Soroban diagnostics covered by #1897.

Unsupported Soroban paths could previously reach codegen, Soroban encoder/decoder logic, spec emission, or LLVM and fail with internal panics, `todo!()`, `unimplemented!()`, Inkwell errors, or LLVM assertions. This PR adds Soroban codegen-side validation so those user-triggerable cases are reported as normal Solang diagnostics before the unsafe paths are reached.

## What changed

- Move unsupported Soroban ABI validation out of `sema` and into the Soroban codegen path.
- Validate unsupported public/external Soroban function parameters and return values before dispatch wrapper generation.
- Validate unsupported public accessor return values before generated accessor code can reach unsupported Soroban lowering.
- Validate unsupported Soroban event argument types before event encoding.
- Guard multiple external return values and unsupported array/struct/string/bytes cases that could otherwise reach Soroban spec, encoder/decoder, Inkwell, or LLVM failures.
- Add precise diagnostics for internal string-helper patterns that could otherwise trigger LLVM/Inkwell failures.
- Keep supported Soroban behavior unchanged
